# GEO report: orchard-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 100/100, Strong

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 23 ÷ 23 × 100 = 100. High = (23 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 100.

Every applicable rule is clear, read from code. The one thing code can't show is whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. I sampled all 4 routes: `/`, `/varieties`, `/visit` and `/account`.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

Nothing is broken. The biggest unknown is the one below, because code can't prove it.

### 1. Confirm real crawlers get through your CDN or firewall
- **Why it matters:** the files are fine, but a firewall in front of the site could still block search crawlers.
- **Where:** outside the repository
- **What the code says:** `Allow: /` (`public/robots.txt:2`)
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** stays 100 if it comes back clear. It would drop if crawlers are blocked.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt valid and reachable | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt`, plain text with valid lines |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers allowed per policy | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt:1-3`. Policy is `allow`. GPTBot and ClaudeBot are blocked (lines 5-9), which matches `trainingCrawlers: block` and isn't scored. |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked routes indexable | Clear | Not run | 3 of 3 sitemap routes have no noindex. `/account` is noindex and not in the sitemap. |
| GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on the declared origin | Clear | Not run | `app/page.tsx:1`, `app/varieties/page.tsx:1`, `app/visit/page.tsx:1`. 3 of 3 indexable routes are clear. |
| GEO-003 | Content in server HTML | Clear | Not run | All pages are server components with text in the markup. |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD valid | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD found |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap discoverable | Clear | Not run | `public/sitemap.xml`, `public/robots.txt:11` |
| GEO-012 | Title, description, lang | Clear | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:5` has `lang="en"`. The 3 indexable routes have a title and description. `/account` has no description, but it's deliberately noindex and I left it out. |
| GEO-016 | Routes reached by server-rendered links | Clear | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:7` uses plain `<a href>` links. |
| GEO-017 | No snippet conflict | Clear | Not run | Only `data-nosnippet` on one element (`app/layout.tsx:9`), which is a deliberate, scoped choice. No `nosnippet` anywhere. |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | Not run | I read the layout and 4 pages. There are no images, and the links have text. |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (info only) | Not scored | Not run | None present |
| GEO-102 | App structured data (info only) | Not scored | Not run | Not an app |

## Other problems found

None found.

## Worth considering

- **Visit page promises directions it doesn't give:** `app/visit/page.tsx:1`: `description: 'Opening times and directions.'`. The page body only says "Open Thursday to Sunday, April to October." Adding an address and directions as text would answer what a visitor comes to ask.
- **Opening times could be labelled for machines:** `app/visit/page.tsx:4`: `Open Thursday to Sunday, April to October.` Once an address is on the page, `LocalBusiness` JSON-LD could label the address and hours.
- **Varieties are a list that could each have a page:** `app/varieties/page.tsx:4`: `Over forty varieties, from Ashmead’s Kernel to Worcester Pearmain.` The claim of forty isn't backed by a list. Giving each variety its own page and address would let people and machines find and cite individual apples.
- **Home page links onward only through the menu:** `app/page.tsx:4`: `Grown in Herefordshire since 1952.` In-text links to the varieties and visit pages would connect the pages for readers.
- **Sitemap has no dates:** `public/sitemap.xml:3`: `<url><loc>https://www.orchard.example/</loc></url>`. If you know when pages really changed, `<lastmod>` could add a useful signal.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>` to check real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Live-only checks:** whether the sitemap URLs answer 200, and whether any `X-Robots-Tag` headers are added outside the repository.

## Assumptions

- You want AI search tools to find the site. This matches `policy.aiSearchCrawlers: allow` in `geo.config.json`.
- `/account` is deliberately private. It has `noindex`, is disallowed in `robots.txt` and isn't in the sitemap.
- Next.js adds the viewport and charset tags by default, so I didn't check them.

## What to do next

1. Nothing needs fixing now, so there's no `fix` run to do.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
